subject: Post-demo: SLO readout and acceptance path for ACME integration
summary: Post-demo qualification: validated ACME latency & streaming needs, confirmed acceptance targets, and agreed on a mutual action plan (MAP) with engineering spikes + a 2-week performance pilot.
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah James <sarah.james@acme.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: SLO readout and acceptance path for ACME integration

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking the time to run through the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

SLOs you called out during the demo (summary):
- End-user streaming latency (p95 response start): <= 120 ms for 1–2 token chunks on the web client at average concurrency of 250
- Backend token throughput: sustained 55k tokens/sec across the inference pool during peak batch windows
- Concurrent active sessions: target 600 active sessions with 1s median first-byte across regions
- Quality regression tolerance: <1.5% measured on your validation prompts (we'll coordinate eval set)

Accept / dev-path proposal:
1) Acceptance criteria doc: we shared a draft checklist (attached: redwood-slo-checklist-v1.pdf). If that aligns, we mark items as pass/fail during the pilot.
2) Performance pilot (2 weeks): Redwood provisions a scoped Dedicated pool with the same model config used in demo; we run a workload replay (you provide sample-load-plan.csv) to validate throughput & latency.
3) Engineering spike: Markus will validate streaming chunk sizes and client-side buffer settings to reproduce the p95 target at your concurrency profile.
4) Rollout gates: canary -> 50% -> full with automatic fallback to quantized variant if latency regressions are observed.

Open items we need from ACME to start pilot:
- Your representative dataset / prompt set for eval (redacted if needed)
- Realistic session concurrency curve (CSV preferred; sample template attached)
- Any network egress limitations (VPC peering/firewall rules) so we pre-validate routing

If this looks good, I suggest we: 1) lock acceptance checklist by end of week (Fri 2026-08-23), and 2) start the pilot the week of 2026-08-31.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up if you prefer to walk through the checklist line-by-line.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-slo-checklist-v1.pdf (pdf, 45KB), sample-load-plan.csv (csv, 2KB)
From: Sarah James <sarah.james@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>, platform@acme.com
Date: 2026-08-21T18:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO readout and acceptance path for ACME integration

Thanks Evelyn — this is very clear and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying points from our infra team: 

1) The 120 ms p95 target is for perceived typing/assistant responsiveness on our web app. We typically send small streaming chunks (1–4 tokens). Will you need us to change client buffering?
2) For throughput, the 55k tokens/sec target is for the US region only during daytime peak — our EU peak is roughly 25% of US.
3) On the session model: 600 active sessions is conservative; if the pilot shows success we expect to scale to 2k sessions in Q4. Any concerns about linearity?

We can provide a redacted prompt set by tomorrow and I'll work with Tom to generate the concurrency CSV. For network, we can open a peered path to the Dedicated pool CIDRs you provide.

Two asks: please have Markus confirm whether your streaming implementation requires changes on our client buffer settings, and can you share the exact model variant and quantization we used in the demo so we can match evaluation conditions?

— Sarah
VP Product, ACME Corporation

Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLO readout and acceptance path for ACME integration

Hi Sarah — looping in answers to your two asks and adding a couple technical notes.

Client buffering and streaming:
- Redwood's streaming uses ~1-token prefetch by default for the client demo; that produced the smoothest perceived latency during the demo. If your client buffers >200ms before rendering, you will see worse p95 even if server-side is fast.
- Recommendation: have your web client render on chunk arrival (1–4 tokens). If that's not possible, a 50–75 ms client flush interval is the next-best option.

Model variant & quantization:
- Demo model: open-model-v2.3 (fp16) with int8 quantized fallback available. For pilot we suggest starting with fp16 to verify quality, then evaluate int8-quant for cost/latency trade-offs.

Throughput and concurrency:
- Linearity: performance is not perfectly linear as token length and KV-cache reuse affect throughput. For 600 -> 2k sessions you should expect ~1.8x capacity needs depending on average token/session. We'll include a capacity estimate in the pilot plan once we have your session length distribution.

Data we need from ACME (action items):
- Redacted prompt set + evaluation labels (scoped subset is fine)
- Concurrency CSV (start/end timestamps + active session counts)

I'll prepare a short runbook to reproduce the demo workload (will attach to the acceptance doc). Proposed spike: 3 engineer-days to tune streaming buffer and measure p95 across concurrency curve.

-Markus
Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-demo-replay.md (txt, 6KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Post-demo: SLO readout and acceptance path for ACME integration

Thanks Sarah — good to see alignment. Quick MAP and owners so it's actionable: 

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — ACME / Redwood
- By 2026-08-25 (ACME): share redacted eval prompts + concurrency CSV (owner: Tom Rivera)
- By 2026-08-26 (Redwood): finalize acceptance checklist (owner: Evelyn) — attached updated checklist link: https://docs.redwood.ai/acceptance-checklist/ACME-42
- 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-14 (Redwood + ACME): 2-week performance pilot (engineers: Markus, Neha) — pilot infra: scoped Dedicated pool; pilot runbook will include traffic replay and live streaming tests
- 2026-09-18 (Joint review): acceptance pass/fail and next pricing/commitment discussion (owners: Evelyn + Sarah)

Dependencies / risks:
- If client buffering isn't adjusted, we may miss the 120 ms p95 despite server improvements — mitigation: short dev spike to instrument client render times during week 1 of pilot.
- If token/session lengths are significantly longer than demo (e.g., multi-turn sessions averaging 1k tokens), throughput needs will increase non-linearly — mitigation: run token-length stratified runs in pilot.

Next steps: Sarah, can you confirm the owner for the CSV and whether 2026-08-25 works to deliver the prompt set? If yes I'll lock the checklist and schedule the pilot infra.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
